items.title: fix: keep cold sessions visible and verify release recovery (#145462)
items.summary: fix: keep cold sessions visible and verify release recovery (#145462) * test: cover transcript cold storage in release Docker lanes * test: remove stale cloud picker test seams Clear baseline CI failures introduced by #145183: reuse the existing picker fixture, test cloud configuration through its production renderer, and remove the unused Connect menu renderer. * test: preserve historical transcript fixture modification times Doctor imports filesystem mutation time rather than timestamps inside messages. Date the legacy files before import, and handle CLI failure diagnostics without adding a lint suppression or retaining credential-bearing command arguments. * fix: keep cold sessions available to Activity title probes Handle cold transcripts at the optional title-reader boundary without restoring payloads or caching missing previews. Verify real archival, mixed hot/cold listings and cache recovery; extend packaged release proof across restart and portable backup recovery. Preserve JSON CLI errors from stdout in the test harness. * fix(ui): use the action cursor for session details Clear the existing cursor-policy failure from #145183 without weakening its regression test. * test: preserve frozen release targets in cold-storage lanes Share capability resolution with source preflight and omit only unsupported cold subcases under the existing explicit frozen-target policy. Keep current coverage required, isolate ordinary retention in the live fixture, and strengthen fixture typing without suppressions. * test: complete cold-storage release entrypoint contracts Register the shell entrypoints for dependency analysis, type the frozen-source fixture cases explicitly, and align existing cloud test callback ordering with the same repair now on main. * test: isolate archived recall from external tool policy * test: retain the cloud machine locator for proof capture

items.title: fix(cli): restore local media inference with saved credential referen…
items.summary: fix(cli): restore local media inference with saved credential references (#144931) Closes #144930. ## What Problem This Solves Local image, embedding, audio, and video inference fail before sending a provider request when the selected agent saves its credential as a SecretRef. Local model inference already prepares the same credential. ## Why This Change Was Made Extend the existing selected-agent account-secret preparation to every local media and embedding runner. Rename the model-only helper to match its shared scope. Keep the preparation behavior, account selection, auth precedence, and storage unchanged. This carries forward @masatohoshino’s repair from #144931 and retains @Bruce-Yii’s shared preparation from #141569. ## User Impact Local media and embedding commands can use the selected agent’s saved credential reference, as local model inference already does. Missing secrets still fail before provider traffic. ## Evidence Real CLI proof uses an isolated state, an account created with `onboard --secret-input-mode ref`, a distinct saved account on another agent, and local protocol-compatible HTTP fixtures. No Gateway or external provider account is used. | Command | Base `f96c900b1d424820c43a184d67694003583581bf` | Head `7ab685a8195d534e22ee52202a2752c178c424de` | | --- | --- | --- | | Embedding create | Exit 1; unmaterialized account reference; zero requests | Exit 0; expected embedding; selected credential at HTTP egress | | Image generate | Exit 1; same error; zero requests | Exit 0; PNG written; selected credential at HTTP egress | | Audio transcribe | Exit 1; same error; zero requests | Exit 0; expected transcript; selected credential at HTTP egress | | Video generate | Exit 1; same error; zero requests | Exit 0; authenticated create/download; fixture bytes written | | Image describe, sole agent | Exit 1; unmaterialized account reference; zero requests | Exit 0; selected credential at HTTP egress; returned image description | | Video describe, sole agent | Exit 1; unmaterialized account reference; zero requests | Exit 0; selected credential at HTTP egress; returned video description | | Local model run | Exit 0; selected credential | Exit 0; selected credential | | Missing selected secret | Exit 1; zero requests | Exit 1; zero requests despite a usable other-agent account | Image proof uses the existing local-image fixture opt-in on both base and head. Audio and video use the existing private-network request opt-in. The original small-audio and image network-policy setup failures are retained in private evidence. An independent source-blind pass confirms successful outputs and selected credentials for all four capability families, zero traffic for each missing-secret case, and the current credential after rotation in a new CLI process. The other-agent account succeeds when selected directly. Description proof retains the real media runtime and provider adapters. Both matched pairs use the same saved account database and command arguments; configs differ only by the local fixture port. Image returns “A synthetic blue square is visible.” Video sends a playable ten-frame input and returns “A synthetic blue square moves across the video.” Removing the selected secret makes each command fail before HTTP. A separate independent audit confirms the captured requests, exact selected credential classification, media payload bytes, outputs, and base/head state comparison. Image description uses a documented sole-agent configuration to isolate secret preparation. The explicit-agent multi-agent image command still fails on both base and head because the separate forwarding defect remains. Those failures are retained. Initial video fixture configuration and endpoint-policy failures are also retained; the qualified proof uses an existing provider adapter that supports a local compatible endpoint. No runtime or auth function is mocked in these description proofs. Limits: HTTP fixtures prove credential routing and output handling, not external provider generation quality. Generated-video output is a synthetic container; its playback is unconfirmed. The playable video above is the description input. The independent pass observed audio model-override behavior outside this credential repair; no forwarding change is included. ## Consumers - `model.ts`: existing local model caller migrates to the shared helper name; Gateway model flow remains unchanged. - `embedding.ts`: `infer embedding create` prepares selected-account secrets before creating its embedding provider. - `image.ts`: generation/edit share one runner; describe/describe-many share another; both prepare before provider auth. - `audio.ts`: transcription prepares before the media runtime. - `video.ts`: generation and description prepare before their respective runtimes. - `local-account-secrets.test.ts`: retains both existing preparation contract tests under the new name. - `capability-cli.test.ts`: mock follows the shared helper rename; command wiring coverage is retained. - `local-runners.account-secrets.test.ts`: six registered command routes reach real SQLite account and secrets owners before mocked provider execution. - Search across source, plugins, UI, native apps and docs finds no other consumer of the retired helper/module names. Provider inventories do not perform inference; TTS and web use separate auth contracts. - Pipeline: registered command → config-reference resolution → selected agent → existing account-secret preparation → provider auth → HTTP request and output. Fixture HTTP headers are the credential proof boundary. ## Invalidation No new cached or persisted state. The existing preparation activates a process-local snapshot only when none exists. Each standalone CLI process rereads the selected account and current secret value. An already active snapshot remains owned by the secrets runtime. Existing tests retain source-config preservation and active-snapshot behavior. Missing-secret and other-agent controls verify owner isolation. Independent rotation checks pass for embedding, image, audio and video in fresh CLI processes. ## Contention No new locks, queues or transactions held. Existing account loading and snapshot activation owners remain unchanged. ## Tests Base `f96c900b1d424820c43a184d67694003583581bf` reproduces unmaterialized account-reference failures for embedding, image generation, image description, audio transcription, video generation and video description: exit 1, zero HTTP requests. The same account succeeds for local model inference. The regression table fails all six cases on the base with `SECRET_SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE`. It invokes the registered image generate/describe, embedding create, audio transcribe and video generate/describe commands. No new production test seam is needed. Targeted validation passes: 316 tests across nine files, including capability commands, the existing model account-secret sibling, lazy registration, and command-secret coverage. Targeted formatting, diff whitespace, file-size and assertion safety checks pass. Full typechecking runs in CI. Test deletion ledger: no behavior deleted. The existing helper test file is renamed with its two cases preserved; the wiring suite mock follows that rename. No baseline or snapshot exceptions. Upgrade behavior: no schema, config, protocol, persistence, updater, Doctor or plugin contract changes; existing credentials and auth precedence are retained. Related open work: #145188 and #145171 repair agent-option forwarding in the same owner files. Their defect is separate; this patch does not duplicate their change. Recheck overlap on the landing merge tree. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
